title: [observability][performance] The gate owner-change batch (a)-(f): stage lines start a line; a check goes to the base only with a test failing in both runs (check-tests --no-fail-fast); a check runs alone before a rejection; check-tests FAILED messages are the panic's or the Python assertion; the relay stall test judged with room on the relay's clock; the jev relay unit's proxy as live
prompt:
Spawn, objective 208 [observability][performance] (the gate owner-change batch (a)-(f) of sync/lead-after-landing.md, listed since 11-16; owner t469u 2026-11-17: ONE contract in its own gate; author rev-e; readers rev-g first, rev-b second). Owner-side only: scripts/, rsi/scenarios/check-tests.sh, deploy/. No fleet code.

lead-mac has no branch in flight on gate.sh/deploy (lead-mac 07:51, the cc-rules line).

Base: live main d8731b17.

(a) Stage lines glued onto scenario output (rev-g, FD 049). gate.sh copied every log into its output with `sed 's/^/| /'` (13 places: job_output, the build, snapshot, metadata, preflight, base build, tests listing, a killed run, sandbox retries). GNU sed keeps a last line that has no newline, so the stage line printed next was glued onto the scenario's last words. New: bar <prefix> [<file>] (awk, every line ends in a newline; the prefix through the environment, since awk -v reads backslashes), used at all 13. FD 050 reads the logs already written; this only stops new gluing.

(b) A check that fails twice compared no tests (rev-f, #28): failing A, then B went to the base and, with the base passing, was a regression. New, in gate.sh's check path: when both candidate runs exit 1 and both name their failing tests (`FAILED <test>:`), and no test is in both (shared_failed), each failing test passed in the other run: the check's own flake rule ("fails once, then passes"), test by test. The check is a flake, accepted and named in `flakes`, and the log names each run's tests. A run that names no test (a build that failed, a crash), or a test in both runs, goes to the base as before. R2 (rev-g's F1 on R1): so does a run with a test binary that ended without naming its failure. With --no-fail-fast a run can abort one binary and still name a failing test in another, and two such runs with different flakes beside the same crash were apart and accepted. failed-tests.awk prints `CRASHED <target>: <status>` for each binary cargo says did not exit successfully with a status other than a failed test's 101 (a signal, another exit), <target> as cargo's `to rerun pass` names it, after the FAILED lines. gate.sh's flake rule needs no CRASHED line in either run. For this to be sound each run must name every failing test: check-tests.sh now runs `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`. Without it, a run stopped at the first failing test binary, so a deterministic break in a later crate could hide behind an earlier flake and the two runs would share nothing.

(c) Checks never ran alone (rev-f, #28; gate.sh solo_run skipped is_check): two failures at load and one base pass rejected. New: with more than one job and the check not on the serial list, a pass on the base sends the candidate to solo_run: once more alone (alone.asked), on a fresh test server. The base's run stays beside the gate's other jobs, as today, so a check that fails on the base too waits for nothing. solo_run says how the base ran ("beside the gate's other runs", where a regression's base runs alone); a base pass at load and a candidate failure alone is still a candidate failure. solo_run's results and words are a regression's: fails alone, a candidate failure (rejected); passes alone, load-sensitive (cannot judge, never accepted); its harness exit, cannot judge. One job, or a check on the serial list: unchanged. The wait for alone.now has no bound of its own, as a regression's has none (rev-g n2): it ends when the other jobs end, and the gate's own timeouts and the runner bound those.
The cost, [performance] (the lead's ruling, 2026-11-17): a run alone waits until every other job of the gate has ended (run_jobs), so on this path (a check failed twice and passes on the base) the verdict waits, after the base's run, for the runs beside it to end, as a numbered scenario's already does. That is up to the rest of the candidate phase's wall time, then the check's run alone. Only this path pays it, and today it is a false rejection, which costs a rejection, a slot strike and a re-gate. Not here (the lead's after-landing list): once a decisive run alone is asked, stop the jobs later in order, since every outcome of it ends the gate.

(d) check-tests.sh's FAILED message took a test's first line of output (rev-f): for a test that prints before it panics, that line, and for the relays' Python-backed self-tests (the panic message is the script's output) the unittest progress line. The parser moves to scripts/rsi/failed-tests.awk, run by check-tests.sh from its own tree (`$controller`). The message is now the panic's own (the first line after `panicked at`). For a Python-backed test it is the first `FAIL:`/`ERROR:` line and the first `...Error: ...`/`...Exception: ...` line after it (`FAIL: test_x (Class.test_x): AssertionError: ...`). The `  in <test>:` lines and every other line are as before. R2 (rev-g n1): a FAIL:/ERROR: line counts as Python only after unittest's `==========` rule, so a Rust test that prints `ERROR: ...` keeps its panic's message.

(e) scripts/model-relay-test.py test_a_stall_ends_at_the_silence_bound_not_at_the_next_keep_alive flaked under load (11-15 17:15, rev-f). The right answer (the attempt ends at the silence bound, 0.5 s) and the bug it guards against (a read waits its whole socket timeout after a keep-alive, ending at the next keep-alive, 0.8 s) were 0.3 s apart. They were judged at 0.7 s on the fake upstream's clock, which counts two loopback transits and the accept. Root fix, not more slack: the bound is 2 s and keep-alives come every 1.9 s, so the answers are 2 s and 3.8 s apart. The time is read on the relay's own clock (record_attempts: each attempt's start) and judged at 2.9 s, 0.9 s from each.

(f) deploy/systemd/spawn-jev-relay.service said https_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:10801. Live needs http://proxy.example.com:8118 (nothing listens on 10801 on the VM; direct egress answers 451), and live has run 8118 since 201's install (11-16 22:16). The repo unit now says 8118, with why. Not changed here: spawn-integrate and spawn-loop say 10801, as their live units do. spawn-model-relay says 10801 in the repo, but its live unit has no proxy line; that is lead-mac's to rule.

Tests, scripts/rsi/test-gate.sh:
- 5a's 'a check that fails twice and passes on the base is a regression' now runs with one job (with_jobs 1). The gate's default is nproc/2 jobs with no test database, and beside other jobs (c) now gives that check a run alone first; the case keeps the serial rule's words on any host.
- 5a-tests (b), one job each: two runs that share no failing test, a flake, accepted and named, never at the base; one test in both runs, rejected after the base; a run that names no test, rejected after the base.
- (R2) a run that also crashed a test binary (a CRASHED line), runs otherwise apart: to the base, rejected, never a flake.
- (R3/R4/R5) each run is checked for itself: a CRASHED line in the second run only, and a second run that names no failing test (rev-b's silent2), go to the base, rejected, never a flake.
- (R5) 5a-nofailfast: the real rsi/scenarios/check-tests.sh, copied with scripts/pg-url.sh and failed-tests.awk beside it, on a two-crate workspace with no dependencies (offline), a failing test in each crate, with only its database stood in (psql and scenario-db.sh answer nothing). It names both crates' failing tests, which only --no-fail-fast gives, and exits 1.
- (R2) 5a-messages: a crash log (rev-g's shape): CRASHED with cargo's target and status, beside the other binary's FAILED test; a binary whose tests failed (exit 101) is no crash; a Rust test printing `ERROR:` keeps its panic's message.
- 5a-newline (a): a check whose first run prints its last words with no newline: its line stands alone in the log, never glued to the stage line.
- 5a-messages (d): failed-tests.awk on two logs: a test that printed before it panicked (the panic's message), a plain panic (as before), and a Python-backed test (its failing Python test and the assertion; its `in` lines still listed).
- 16b (the first failure in order is the verdict, early, and the runs after it stopped): its failing check-062.sh now fails on the base too (a host fault, no run alone), so the early verdict and the stopping are still tested; a check that passes on the base now waits to run alone (the cost above).
- (c) gives a check solo_run's verdicts, all of them. A check that fails alone and runs slower alone is rejected as 'slower', as a scenario is (rev-b's note on R4); before 208, a check never ran alone.
- 5a-alone (c), at 4 jobs (class_judge), a scheduled check-zz.sh: fails at load and passes alone, load-sensitive (cannot judge, exit 6, never rejected); fails alone too, rejected 'candidate failure, alone too'; on the serial list, rejected with no run alone.
- (e) is its own test: python3 -I scripts/model-relay-test.py (the 31 tests). A mutant relay that waits the whole silence bound on each read fails it (3.83 s, not under 2.9 s), as it failed the old one. The test passes 3 of 3 on one CPU beside two busy loops.

Verified by: the gate runs check-test-gate.sh (the whole test-gate.sh) and check-tests.sh on the candidate. After landing, the lead reads the next gate log for stage lines that start a line, and the next check-tests FAILED line of a Python-backed test.
